fields.name: Aglao Lahar Trail to Camp Aglao Riverside
fields.description: The primary trekking route to Lake Mapanuepe. From the Barangay Aglao registration point, trekkers follow the volcanic lahar riverbed northwest, crossing three stream channels before arriving at Camp Aglao Riverside on the southeastern lakeshore — the closest camp to the Aglao jump-off. Loose volcanic sand is physically demanding; proper trekking shoes and at least 2L of water required. Local Aeta guide strongly recommended — no trail markers exist. DO NOT swim in the lake (mercury contamination).

fields.name: Aglao Boat Crossing to Sunken Church Camp
fields.description: Board an outrigger banca at the Aglao View Deck port and cross the lake to Sunken Church Camp on the western shore — the camp closest to the iconic steeple of Sta. Barbara's Chapel (Bojaoen Church), the submerged visita of Barangay Buhawen. The 15-minute dawn crossing is mist-covered and atmospheric. Life vests mandatory, max 5 per banca.

fields.name: Buhawen Alternate Trail to Camp Silingan
fields.description: An alternate overland entry to Lake Mapanuepe from Barangay Buhawen on the southwestern side. Less crowded than Aglao, passes through cogon grasslands, a remnant forest patch, old Buhawen barangay ruins, and one river crossing before arriving at Camp Silingan on the southwestern shore. A local Buhawen guide is mandatory — the trail is completely unmarked and forks multiple times through tall grass.

fields.name: Central Lahar Trail to Camp Rizal
fields.description: A variant of the main Aglao lahar trail that diverges at the third river crossing and heads toward the central lakeshore, arriving at Camp Rizal — named after the open Rizal grassland area on the central western bank. This section of shore offers wide panoramic views of the entire lake including the sunken church steeple to the south and the New Zealand hills to the north. Moderate tree cover. Local guide essential.

fields.name: Aglao Boat Crossing to Phase 3 Grassland Camp
fields.description: Lake crossing by outrigger banca from the Aglao View Deck to Phase 3 Grassland Camp on the northern shore — the 'New Zealand of Zambales' grassy flatlands with wide open views and agoho-covered hills. Passes the Sunken Church steeple en route. Best experienced at dawn for glassy water. Life vests mandatory, max 5 per banca.

fields.name: Aglao Boat Crossing to Eagles Paradise Camp
fields.description: Lake crossing by outrigger banca from Aglao View Deck to Eagles Paradise Camp — the furthest accessible camp by boat, nestled beneath agoho-covered rolling hills on the northern lakeshore. The most scenic camp on the lake. Eagles and native birds regularly spotted in the surrounding hills. Life vests mandatory, max 5 per banca.

fields.name: New Zealand Ridge Hike to Camp Kuta
fields.description: A steep hike from the Phase 3 Grassland lakeshore up the volcanic ridge to Camp Kuta — the highest campsite at Lake Mapanuepe, located on the 'New Zealand' hilltop ridge. Named after a fortified high point, Camp Kuta offers 360° panoramic views: lake, rolling hills, lahar plains, and the distant Zambales mountain range. Expert level — crumbly volcanic scree, no shade on ascent. Sunrise start strongly recommended.

fields.name: Eagles Paradise Extension Trail to Far Camp
fields.description: An extension trail from Eagles Paradise Camp deeper into the northern lakeshore, reaching Far Camp — the most remote and secluded campsite at Lake Mapanuepe. Not accessible by boat; must be done on foot along the northern bank. Passes through open cogon grassland, an agoho-covered ridge crossing, and a secluded cove approach. No caretaker at Far Camp — self-sufficient campers only. Absolute Leave No Trace required.

fields.name: Aglao Lahar Trail → Camp Aglao Riverside
fields.description: The primary overland trekking route to Camp Aglao Riverside. From the Barangay Aglao registration point, trekkers follow the volcanic lahar riverbed northwest, crossing two stream channels before arriving at the camp on the southeastern lakeshore — the closest campsite to the jump-off. Loose volcanic sand is physically demanding. Local Aeta guide required — no trail markers exist.

fields.name: Buhawen Long Loop → Camp Aglao Riverside
fields.description: A challenging long-loop route starting from Barangay Buhawen, traversing the southwestern lahar flats, crossing the Buhawen river tributary, and looping around the southern lakeshore to arrive at Camp Aglao Riverside from the west. The longest and most demanding route to this camp. Used by experienced trekkers who want a full traverse of the Mapanuepe basin. Buhawen guide required for the first half; Aglao guide takes over at the merge point.

fields.name: Aglao Boat Crossing → Sunken Church Camp
fields.description: The fastest and easiest route to Sunken Church Camp — a 15-minute outrigger banca crossing from the Aglao View Deck port directly to the western lakeshore camp facing the iconic Sta. Barbara steeple. The dawn crossing is mist-covered and atmospheric. Life vests mandatory, max 5 per banca. Best route for day-trippers.

fields.name: Aglao Riverside Shoreline Walk → Sunken Church Camp
fields.description: A flat shoreline walk from Camp Aglao Riverside along the southeastern and western lakeshore to Sunken Church Camp. Follows the lake's rocky and grassy bank closely, passing through an agoho grove and arriving at the viewpoint facing the steeple. Best at sunrise when the cross reflects on the still water. Easy and suitable for all fitness levels.

fields.name: Buhawen Overland Trail → Sunken Church Camp
fields.description: Overland entry from Barangay Buhawen directly to Sunken Church Camp on the western shore. Passes through the old Buhawen ruins, cogon grasslands, and the Buhawen river crossing before arriving at the camp from the south. Less crowded than any Aglao route. Local Buhawen Aeta guide mandatory — no trail markers exist.

fields.name: Buhawen Overland Trail → Camp Silingan
fields.description: The primary overland route to Camp Silingan from Barangay Buhawen on the southwestern side of the lake. Passes through cogon grasslands, old Buhawen ruins, and a river crossing before arriving at Camp Silingan on the southwestern shore. The quietest and least visited of all routes. Local Buhawen Aeta guide mandatory.

fields.name: Aglao Boat Crossing → Camp Silingan
fields.description: Lake crossing by outrigger banca from Aglao View Deck to Camp Silingan on the southwestern shore. Passes the Sunken Church steeple en route. Faster than the overland trail but requires boat hire. Life vests mandatory, max 5 per banca.

fields.name: Sunken Church Shoreline Walk → Camp Silingan
fields.description: A short flat shoreline walk from Sunken Church Camp southward along the western lakeshore to Camp Silingan. The two camps are the closest pair on the lake — good for trekkers who want to explore multiple sites in a day. Flat, easy, and follows the lake bank closely.

fields.name: Sunken Church Shoreline Walk → Camp Silingan

fields.name: Sunken Church Shoreline Walk → Camp Silingan

fields.name: Aglao Central Lahar Trail → Camp Rizal
fields.description: A lahar overland trail from Barangay Aglao that diverges from the main Route 1 at the central fork and heads toward the central western shore arriving at Camp Rizal. Wide panoramic views of the entire lake including the sunken church to the south and New Zealand hills to the north. Local guide essential — fork is completely unmarked.

fields.name: Aglao Boat Crossing → Camp Rizal
fields.description: Lake crossing by outrigger banca from Aglao View Deck to Camp Rizal on the central western shore. Faster than the overland trail — good option for those with heavy gear. Passes the Sunken Church steeple en route. Life vests mandatory, max 5 per banca.

fields.name: Camp Silingan Shoreline Walk → Camp Rizal
fields.description: A flat northern shoreline walk from Camp Silingan to Camp Rizal along the western lakeshore. Connects two adjacent camps for trekkers who want to explore multiple campsites. Flat terrain, excellent continuous lake views, passes rocky outcrops and agoho groves.

fields.name: Aglao Boat Crossing → Phase 3 Grassland Camp
fields.description: Lake crossing by outrigger banca from Aglao View Deck to Phase 3 Grassland Camp — the iconic 'New Zealand of Zambales' grassy flatlands. Passes the Sunken Church steeple. Best at dawn for glassy water. Life vests mandatory, max 5 per banca.

fields.name: Camp Rizal Shoreline Walk → Phase 3 Grassland Camp
fields.description: A flat northern shoreline walk from Camp Rizal continuing along the western lakeshore to Phase 3 Grassland Camp. Passes through agoho groves and open grassy sections. Good inter-camp connector for trekkers hopping between sites. Excellent continuous lake views.

fields.name: Aglao Lahar + Shore Traverse → Phase 3 Grassland Camp
fields.description: A full overland traverse combining the Aglao lahar trail and the western shore walk to reach Phase 3 Grassland Camp entirely on foot — no boat required. The longest single-day trek in the Mapanuepe system. Passes Camp Aglao Riverside and Camp Rizal en route. Recommended only for fit trekkers with full-day availability. Start before 5 AM.

fields.name: Aglao Boat Crossing → Eagles Paradise
fields.description: Lake crossing by outrigger banca from Aglao View Deck to Eagles Paradise Camp — the furthest boat-accessible camp, nestled under agoho-covered rolling hills. Eagles and native birds regularly spotted. Life vests mandatory, max 5 per banca.

fields.name: Phase 3 Grassland Walk → Eagles Paradise
fields.description: A short northern shoreline walk from Phase 3 Grassland Camp to Eagles Paradise along the northern lakeshore. Connects the two most popular northern camps. Flat grassy terrain with agoho views the entire way. Great inter-camp connector route.

fields.name: Phase 3 Grassland Walk → Eagles Paradise
fields.description: A short northern shoreline walk from Phase 3 Grassland Camp to Eagles Paradise along the northern lakeshore. Connects the two most popular northern camps. Flat grassy terrain with agoho views the entire way. Great inter-camp connector route.

fields.name: Full Overland Traverse → Eagles Paradise
fields.description: The ultimate Mapanuepe full overland trek — from Barangay Aglao through the entire lahar trail system, along the complete western lakeshore, passing all intermediate camps to arrive at Eagles Paradise entirely on foot. No boat required. 7.5 km total. Only for experienced trekkers with full-day availability and excellent physical condition. Start no later than 4 AM. Two guides recommended.

fields.name: Phase 3 Ridge Hike → Camp Kuta
fields.description: Steep ascent from Phase 3 Grassland Camp up the volcanic ridge to Camp Kuta — the highest campsite at Lake Mapanuepe with 360° panoramic views. Crumbly volcanic scree, exposed knife ridge near the summit, no shade on ascent. Expert level — sunrise start strongly recommended. No water source at summit; carry all water up.

fields.name: Eagles Paradise Ridge Hike → Camp Kuta
fields.description: A shorter but still steep ridge ascent from Eagles Paradise Camp to Camp Kuta along the eastern face of the ridge. Slightly less exposed than the Phase 3 approach but still requires good fitness and grip footwear. The eastern face offers different lake angles during the ascent. Best used as a return variation after summiting via the Phase 3 route.

fields.name: Eagles Paradise Extension → Far Camp
fields.description: The primary and only overland route to Far Camp — the most remote campsite at Lake Mapanuepe. From Eagles Paradise, follow the northern lakeshore through cogon grassland, over an agoho ridge, and down into the secluded Far Camp cove. Not accessible by boat. No caretaker, no facilities — self-sufficient campers only. Leave No Trace required.

fields.name: Camp Kuta North Descent → Far Camp
fields.description: A descent from Camp Kuta summit down the northern face of the ridge to Far Camp below. Used primarily as a route variation by trekkers who have camped at Kuta and want to descend to the remote Far Camp cove. Steep rocky descent on loose volcanic soil — trekking poles essential and face the slope when descending the steeper sections.

fields.name: Full Northern Loop → Far Camp
fields.description: An expert-level northern loop from Phase 3 Grassland Camp, ascending Camp Kuta summit then descending the north face to Far Camp. Combines the ridge summit experience with arrival at the most remote camp. Panoramic views from the Kuta summit en route. Full supplies and two guides required. Recommended for experienced groups only.
